items.title: Saylor Says Strategy Intends To Buy All Remaining Bitcoin
points: MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor publicly stated the company intends to purchase all remaining Bitcoin not currently owned by other entities
This aggressive accumulation strategy reflects continued corporate interest in Bitcoin as a long-term store of value (store of value: an asset that reliably maintains its purchasing power over time)
The announcement signals confidence in Bitcoin's future despite ongoing regulatory and market uncertainties

items.title: DOJ Seeks $1.17B in Stolen USDC from Binance Hack
points: DOJ seeks $1.17B in stolen USDC (a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar) tied to a Binance hack attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group and APT38, across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains; theft occurred October 29
Circle blocked the stolen tokens and agreed to issue equivalent replacement USDC to the US if a judge grants forfeiture

DOJ reports $2.9B+ in total crypto frozen, seized, or returned since the theft; Binance reports $6.34B in losses, claims replenishment completed, and secured a $6.5B worldwide freezing order in Abu Dhabi

items.title: Visa Launches CLI Agent Wallet
points: Visa launched CLI, an experimental agent wallet on Tempo and Machine Payments Protocol, letting US users attach Visa cards to AI agent wallets for paid tasks in video, music, gaming, and surveys, earning OUSD stablecoin
Agents register in Visa's directory for verified task completion; Visa positions its 5B payment credentials as an accountability layer for agent transactions

Daydreams' TaskMarket on Base and Tempo has 16,500 registered agents, 1,843 tasks, and $3,756 paid out; Tempo serves as a settlement layer reducing lock-in risk compared to closed platforms like Stripe

items.title: XMR1 Wrapped Monero Collapse
points: XMR1 wrapped Monero token (a token representing Monero on another blockchain) collapsed 99% in 30 minutes after an attacker stole the deployer key via a breach of web host 1984.hosting
Attacker drained 5.2M tokens, sold 364K for $13.5M, and converted proceeds to roughly 7,350 ETH, seeding an exploit wallet via the Tornado Cash mixer

Same deployer account still controls ZEC1 (wrapped Zcash) with identical centralization risk; Wagyu founder pledged direct refunds with no relaunch timeline given; this is Wagyu's second breach in two months

items.title: CFTC Advisory on Crypto Collateral
points: CFTC staff advisory allows crypto derivatives firms to count Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins (subject to a haircut, meaning a discount applied to their value) toward one year of operating expenses, though not toward liquidity requirements

items.title: Chainflip $12M Vault Hack
points: Chainflip confirmed a $12M vault hack draining 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25M USDC, and 758,141 USDT — more than double the initial $4.86M estimate
Protocol offered the attacker a 10% bounty for fund recovery

items.title: Bitcoin ETF Outflows
points: Bitcoin ETFs posted a $1.79B weekly outflow last week, the third-largest on record since the January 2024 launch, extending a four-week redemption streak to $4.34B total outflows

items.title: Block Size and Technical Scaling Constraints
points: Under Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade's 60M gas limit, skipped EIP-7702 authorizations (transaction pre-approvals stored on-chain) represent the worst-case block-size attack, packing 17.0 bytes per 1k gas and producing 1.81 MiB execution layer blocks — about 2x what calldata (transaction input data) achieves

A structural conflict exists with FOCIL (EIP-7805): a transaction satisfying gas constraints may breach the 8 MiB execution layer byte cap when added to a block, leaving builders unable to meet attesters' (validators providing inclusion guarantees) expectations despite valid gas usage

Author proposes pricing every payload byte in gas via EIP-8131 and EIP-8279 plus deposit-request metering with a capped gas limit to bound worst-case envelope size, giving the consensus layer a deterministic maximum: max_envelope_size = C + ceil(1.25 × gas_limit / 64)
